title: Choose the visual world for AI System Design
question: The roll assigned Drawing Set. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Drawing Set
options.lineage: cyanotype engineering drawing sets and their title blocks
options.thesis: The course as an issued drawing set: every lesson is a numbered sheet of one system, Relay.
options.viewport: Home is the cover sheet: Prussian-blue field, the course title in a drawing title block, and a sheet index of the six weeks as numbered sheet groups. A lesson opens on whiteprint with its own title block (sheet number, time, status, last checked) beside a calm reading column.
options.risk: Blueprints are the obvious reading of 'system design'; set timidly it becomes clip-art blueprint wallpaper.

raised.raise: Every number in the course (costs, latencies, token math) sets in tabular monospace columns with full commitment, like dimension strings.
The six weeks are discrete labelled phases of the set, never a colour-only progression.
One accent colour, redline red, is reserved for 'you are here' and the single next action; nothing else may use it.
Completion is a permanent mark: a finished sheet gets a CHECKED stamp in its title block that stays.

options.label: Six Lines to Production
options.thesis: Each week is a coloured line, each lesson a station, and Relay is the train that rides all six.
options.viewport: Home is the network map with your current station lit; a lesson page shows its line strip across the top like a platform sign.
options.risk: Familiar: course roadmaps drawn as transit maps are common, and six line colours compete with diagrams.

options.label: Patent Drawing Sheet
options.thesis: Every lesson is a figure of one invention, its parts numbered and leader-linked to the text that explains them.
options.viewport: A lesson opens as FIG. 3 of the Relay specification, with numbered parts whose leaders point to the paragraphs that explain them.
options.case: Fuses well: numbered system diagrams tied to the text are a real reading aid; loses narrowly on audience identification.
options.risk: Patent sheets read as legal and cold to some readers.

options.label: Cutting Bench Rail
options.thesis: The course as a perforated rail of frames, with a folded flag exactly where you stopped.
options.viewport: A rail of 36 frames crosses the top of every page; your flag sits on the lesson you left, and finished frames carry a grease cross.
options.case: Fuses partly: 'resume where you stopped' maps perfectly to progress; engineers do not identify with film editing.
options.risk: Orange-on-black at a third of the screen is tiring over a 50-minute lesson.

options.label: Data-sublime field
options.thesis: The course as a barcode field of pure black and white data.
options.viewport: A barcode lattice with dense numbers in the margin.
options.case: Fuses poorly: strobing data fields fight 50-minute reading sessions.
options.kept: Numbers set with total tabular commitment.

options.label: Cyclorama dawn
options.thesis: Weeks as lighting phases from night to day.
options.viewport: A dark-to-light horizon rising as you progress.

options.label: Drawcord cape
options.thesis: One gold cord transforms a flat plane into structure.
options.viewport: A black field with one gold control line.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no tie to engineers or the course.
options.risk: Fashion costume on a technical course.
options.kept: One accent reserved for the single control.

options.label: Sticker accretion
options.case: Fuses poorly: illegibility is the point of the source.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.viewport: Left navigation, centred article, on-this-page rail, the arrangement every docs reader expects.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other course and docs site by design.
